source.text: Καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον, ἔχον κέρατα δέκα καὶ κεφαλὰς ἑπτά, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν κεράτων αὐτοῦ δέκα διαδήματα, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ὀνόματα βλασφημίας.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw out of the sea a beast coming up, having horns ten and heads seven, and on the horns of it ten diadems, and on the heads of it names of blasphemy.

en.L: And I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns ten royal crowns, and on its heads names of blasphemy.
en.B: Then I saw a beast rising out of the sea. It had ten horns and seven heads, ten royal crowns on its horns, and on its heads names that blasphemed God.
en.R: Then I saw a beast coming up out of the sea. It had ten horns and seven heads. There was a king's crown on each horn. On each head was a name that insulted God.

fr.L: Et je vis, montant de la mer, une bête ayant dix cornes et sept têtes, et sur ses cornes dix diadèmes, et sur ses têtes des noms de blasphème.
fr.B: Puis je vis une bête qui montait de la mer. Elle avait dix cornes et sept têtes, dix diadèmes sur ses cornes, et sur ses têtes des noms qui blasphémaient Dieu.
fr.R: Puis j’ai vu une bête qui sortait de la mer. Elle avait dix cornes et sept têtes. Il y avait une couronne de roi sur chaque corne. Sur chaque tête, il y avait un nom qui insultait Dieu.

es.L: Y vi una bestia que subía del mar, que tenía diez cuernos y siete cabezas, y sobre sus cuernos diez diademas, y sobre sus cabezas nombres de blasfemia.
es.B: Entonces vi una bestia que subía del mar. Tenía diez cuernos y siete cabezas, diez diademas sobre sus cuernos, y sobre sus cabezas nombres que blasfemaban contra Dios.
es.R: Luego vi una bestia que salía del mar. Tenía diez cuernos y siete cabezas. En cada cuerno había una corona de rey. En cada cabeza tenía un nombre que insultaba a Dios.

sw.L: Na nikamwona mnyama akipanda kutoka baharini, mwenye pembe kumi na vichwa saba, na juu ya pembe zake taji kumi za kifalme, na juu ya vichwa vyake majina ya kufuru.
sw.B: Kisha nikamwona mnyama akipanda kutoka baharini. Alikuwa na pembe kumi na vichwa saba, taji kumi za kifalme juu ya pembe zake, na juu ya vichwa vyake majina ya kumkufuru Mungu.
sw.R: Kisha nikamwona mnyama akitoka baharini. Alikuwa na pembe kumi na vichwa saba. Kulikuwa na taji ya kifalme juu ya kila pembe. Juu ya kila kichwa kulikuwa na jina lililomtukana Mungu.

decisions.choice: a beast from the sea: Daniel 7
decisions.reason: Daniel saw four great beasts come up out of the sea, the fourth with ten horns, and was told that they are kingdoms (Daniel 7:2-8, 17, 23-24). The sea stood for the chaotic powers opposed to God. This beast has the dragon's heads and horns (12:3): it is his agent.

decisions.choice: the beast: a power that opposes God and demands worship
alternatives: the Roman Empire and its emperors in John's day
a recurring pattern of state power set against God
a final ruler at the end of history
decisions.reason: Many features point to Rome as John's readers knew it: emperors who claimed divine titles, worship of the emperor in the cities of Asia, and the city on seven hills (17:9). Many readers also see in the beast a pattern that recurs wherever earthly power claims what belongs to God, and some a final figure at the end. The text uses symbols and does not name it.

decisions.choice: names of blasphemy: titles that claim divine honor
decisions.reason: The beast bears names that insult God by claiming what is his. Roman emperors were given titles such as "divine", "son of god" and "lord".

decisions.choice: it, its: the beast
decisions.reason: θηρίον is neuter, and every level calls the beast "it".

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R): "je vis" / "j’ai vu"; historic presents kept at Literal ("elle exerce", "elle fait", "elle égare")
alternatives: the present of narration at Balanced, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: John tells what he saw. Where Greek describes what the second beast keeps doing in the present (13:12-16), Literal keeps the present, Balanced uses the imperfect, the French tense for ongoing action in a past narrative, and Readable the passé composé. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: la bête, with "elle", "sa", "ses" (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: French "bête" is feminine, so the beast is "elle" where the English says "it"; the neuter Greek has no French equivalent. "La bête" is the familiar word and keeps the link with Daniel 7 (m1); "monstre" would add a judgment the word does not make.

decisions.choice: nombres de blasfemia (L); nombres que blasfemaban contra Dios (B); un nombre que insultaba a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: "Blasfemia" is the settled Spanish word for speech against God, and these names claim divine honor, as the meaning decision says. Readable says it plainly with "insultar a Dios", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: majina ya kufuru (L); majina ya kumkufuru Mungu (B); jina lililomtukana Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kufuru" is blasphemy against God, as settled for the Swahili New Testament: titles that claim divine honour (m3). Readable says the names insulted God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: mnyama, with personal agreement
decisions.reason: The beast is "mnyama" as in 11:7; Swahili gives it the personal prefixes ("alikuwa", "akipanda"), as for any animal, so the English "it" has no separate counterpart.

source.text: καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδον ἦν ὅμοιον παρδάλει, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς ἄρκου, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ὡς στόμα λέοντος.

records.literal_gloss: And the beast which I saw was like to a leopard, and the feet of it as of a bear, and the mouth of it as mouth of a lion.

en.L: And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet [were] like a bear's, and its mouth like a lion's mouth.
en.B: The beast I saw was like a leopard; its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion.
en.R: The beast looked like a leopard. But it had feet like a bear and a mouth like a lion.

fr.L: Et la bête que je vis était semblable à un léopard, et ses pieds [étaient] comme ceux d’un ours, et sa gueule comme la gueule d’un lion.
fr.B: La bête que je vis ressemblait à un léopard ; ses pattes étaient comme celles d’un ours, et sa gueule comme la gueule d’un lion.
fr.R: La bête ressemblait à un léopard. Mais elle avait des pattes d’ours et une gueule de lion.

es.L: Y la bestia que vi era semejante a un leopardo, y sus pies [eran] como de oso, y su boca como boca de león.
es.B: La bestia que vi parecía un leopardo; sus pies eran como los de un oso, y su boca como la de un león.
es.R: La bestia parecía un leopardo. Pero tenía patas de oso y boca de león.

sw.L: Na yule mnyama niliyemwona alikuwa kama chui, na miguu yake [ilikuwa] kama ya dubu, na kinywa chake kama kinywa cha simba.
sw.B: Yule mnyama niliyemwona alifanana na chui; miguu yake ilikuwa kama ya dubu, na kinywa chake kama kinywa cha simba.
sw.R: Mnyama huyo alionekana kama chui. Lakini alikuwa na miguu kama ya dubu na kinywa kama cha simba.

decisions.choice: leopard, bear and lion: Daniel's beasts in one
decisions.reason: Daniel's first three beasts were like a lion, a bear and a leopard (Daniel 7:4-6). John's beast combines them, in reverse order: it gathers up all the empires that went before.

decisions.choice: la gueule (13:2); la bouche where the beast speaks (13:5-6)
decisions.reason: French uses "gueule" for an animal's mouth, which suits the picture of the lion; where the mouth speaks great things and blasphemies, "bouche" is the word for speech.

source.text: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ δράκων τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην.

records.literal_gloss: And gave to it the dragon the power of him and the throne of him and authority great.

en.L: And the dragon gave it his power and his throne and great authority.
en.B: The dragon handed over to it his power, his throne, and great authority.
en.R: The dragon gave the beast his own power, his throne, and great authority.

fr.L: Et le dragon lui donna sa puissance et son trône et une grande autorité.
fr.B: Le dragon lui remit sa puissance, son trône et une grande autorité.
fr.R: Le dragon a donné à la bête sa propre puissance, son trône et une grande autorité.

es.L: Y el dragón le dio su poder y su trono y gran autoridad.
es.B: El dragón le entregó su poder, su trono y gran autoridad.
es.R: El dragón le dio a la bestia su propio poder, su trono y mucha autoridad.

sw.L: Na yule joka akampa uweza wake na kiti chake cha enzi na mamlaka makuu.
sw.B: Joka akamkabidhi uweza wake, kiti chake cha enzi na mamlaka makuu.
sw.R: Joka akampa mnyama huyo uweza wake mwenyewe, kiti chake cha enzi, na mamlaka makuu.

decisions.choice: the dragon's gift: a parody of the Father's gift to the Son
decisions.reason: The devil claimed to have the authority of the world's kingdoms to give (Luke 4:5-6). As the Father gives authority to the Son (2:27-28; 5:7), the dragon gives his throne to the beast.

source.text: καὶ μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεφαλῶν αὐτοῦ ὡς ἐσφαγμένην εἰς θάνατον, καὶ ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐθεραπεύθη.

records.literal_gloss: And one of the heads of it as having been slaughtered to death, and the wound of the death of it was healed.

en.L: And one of its heads [was] as though slaughtered to death, and its death-wound was healed.
en.B: One of its heads looked as though it had been slaughtered and killed, but its deadly wound had been healed.
en.R: One of the beast's heads looked as if it had been killed. But the deadly wound had healed.

fr.L: Et l’une de ses têtes [était] comme égorgée à mort, et sa blessure mortelle fut guérie.
fr.B: L’une de ses têtes semblait avoir été égorgée, frappée à mort, mais sa blessure mortelle avait été guérie.
fr.R: Une des têtes de la bête avait l’air d’avoir été tuée. Mais la blessure mortelle avait guéri.

es.L: Y una de sus cabezas [estaba] como degollada de muerte, y su herida de muerte fue sanada.
es.B: Una de sus cabezas parecía haber sido degollada y muerta, pero su herida mortal había sido sanada.
es.R: Una de las cabezas de la bestia parecía haber sido herida de muerte. Pero esa herida mortal se había curado.

sw.L: Na kimoja cha vichwa vyake [kilikuwa] kama kilichochinjwa hata kufa, na jeraha lake la kifo likapona.
sw.B: Kimoja cha vichwa vyake kilionekana kama kilichochinjwa kikauawa, lakini jeraha lake la kuua lilikuwa limepona.
sw.R: Kimoja cha vichwa vya mnyama huyo kilionekana kama kilikuwa kimeuawa. Lakini jeraha hilo la kuua lilikuwa limepona.

decisions.choice: as though slaughtered, and healed: a parody of the Lamb
decisions.reason: ὡς ἐσφαγμένην are the words used of the Lamb, "as though slaughtered" (5:6). The beast imitates the death and resurrection of Christ, to win the world's wonder (13:3-4, 14).

decisions.choice: a wounded head that recovers: perhaps the legend of Nero's return
decisions.reason: After the emperor Nero died by his own hand in AD 68, rumors spread that he was alive and would return, and pretenders arose (Tacitus, Histories 2.8; Suetonius, Nero 57). Some see that legend behind the healed head; others see the recovery of the empire after the civil wars of AD 68-69. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: égorgée (L, B)
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the Lamb "égorgé" (5:6, 13:8), and the beast's wound is a parody of it (m1); "égorgée" keeps the echo at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "tuée", as the English says "killed".

decisions.choice: degollada
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is the same one used of the Lamb "como degollado" in 5:6, and the meaning decision reads the beast's wound as a parody of the Lamb; Spanish keeps the same verb at Literal and Balanced so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: kilichochinjwa
decisions.reason: The same verb "kuchinja" (slaughter) as for the Lamb "aliyechinjwa" in 5:6, so that the beast's wound is heard as a parody of the Lamb (m1).

source.text: καὶ ἐθαυμάσθη ὅλη ἡ γῆ ὀπίσω τοῦ θηρίου, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ δράκοντι ὅτι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ λέγοντες· Τίς ὅμοιος τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ τίς δύναται πολεμῆσαι μετ’ αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: And marveled whole the earth after the beast, \v 4 and they worshiped the dragon because he gave the authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast saying: Who [is] like to the beast, and who is able to make war with it?

en.L: And the whole earth marveled [and followed] after the beast, \v 4 and they worshiped the dragon because he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast, and who can make war with it?"
en.B: In amazement the whole earth went after the beast. \v 4 They worshiped the dragon, since he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast as well, saying, "Who is equal to the beast? Who could fight a war against it?"
en.R: The whole world was amazed and followed the beast. \v 4 People worshiped the dragon because he had given his power to the beast. They also worshiped the beast. They said, "Who is as great as the beast? Who can fight against it?"

fr.L: Et la terre entière fut dans l’admiration [et suivit] la bête, \v 4 et ils adorèrent le dragon parce qu’il avait donné l’autorité à la bête, et ils adorèrent la bête, en disant : « Qui est semblable à la bête, et qui peut lui faire la guerre ? »
fr.B: Émerveillée, la terre entière se mit à suivre la bête. \v 4 Les gens adorèrent le dragon, parce qu’il avait donné son autorité à la bête, et ils adorèrent aussi la bête, en disant : « Qui est l’égal de la bête ? Qui pourrait lui faire la guerre ? »
fr.R: Le monde entier a été émerveillé et a suivi la bête. \v 4 Les gens ont adoré le dragon parce qu’il avait donné son pouvoir à la bête. Ils ont aussi adoré la bête. Ils disaient : « Qui est aussi grand que la bête ? Qui peut se battre contre elle ? »

es.L: Y toda la tierra se maravilló [y siguió] tras la bestia, \v 4 y adoraron al dragón porque había dado la autoridad a la bestia, y adoraron a la bestia, diciendo: «¿Quién [es] semejante a la bestia, y quién puede hacer guerra contra ella?».
es.B: El mundo entero, asombrado, se fue tras la bestia. \v 4 Adoraron al dragón, porque había dado su autoridad a la bestia, y adoraron también a la bestia, diciendo: «¿Quién es igual a la bestia? ¿Quién podría hacerle la guerra?».
es.R: El mundo entero se asombró y siguió a la bestia. \v 4 La gente adoró al dragón porque le había dado su poder a la bestia. También adoraron a la bestia. Decían: «¿Quién es tan grande como la bestia? ¿Quién puede pelear contra ella?».

sw.L: Na dunia yote ikamstaajabia mnyama [na kumfuata], \v 4 nao wakamwabudu yule joka kwa sababu alikuwa amempa mnyama mamlaka yake, nao wakamwabudu mnyama, wakisema, "Ni nani aliye kama mnyama, na ni nani awezaye kupigana vita naye?"
sw.B: Dunia yote ikastaajabu, ikamfuata mnyama. \v 4 Wakamwabudu joka kwa sababu alikuwa amempa mnyama mamlaka yake, nao wakamwabudu mnyama pia, wakisema, "Ni nani anayelingana na mnyama? Ni nani awezaye kupigana vita naye?"
sw.R: Watu wa dunia yote walishangaa, wakamfuata mnyama. \v 4 Watu walimwabudu joka kwa sababu alikuwa amempa mnyama uwezo wake. Walimwabudu mnyama pia. Walisema, "Ni nani aliye mkuu kama mnyama huyu? Ni nani anayeweza kupigana naye?"

decisions.choice: Who is like the beast? A parody of praise to God
decisions.reason: Israel sang, "Who is like you, O LORD, among the gods?" (Exodus 15:11; compare Psalm 89:7-9). The name Michael (12:7) means "Who is like God?" The world gives the beast the praise that belongs to God.

decisions.choice: marveled after the beast: wondered and followed
decisions.reason: "Marveled after" packs two ideas: they were amazed and went after it as followers.

source.text: Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ποιῆσαι μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο.

records.literal_gloss: And was given to it a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and was given to it authority to act months forty-two.

en.L: And a mouth was given to it speaking great things and blasphemies, and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months.
en.B: It was allowed a mouth that spoke boastful words and blasphemies, and it was given authority to act for forty-two months.
en.R: The beast was allowed to say proud things and to insult God. It was given power to do what it wanted for forty-two months.

fr.L: Et il lui fut donné une bouche qui proférait de grandes choses et des blasphèmes, et il lui fut donné autorité d’agir quarante-deux mois.
fr.B: Il lui fut accordé une bouche qui proférait des paroles orgueilleuses et des blasphèmes, et elle reçut le pouvoir d’agir pendant quarante-deux mois.
fr.R: La bête a pu dire des choses pleines d’orgueil et insulter Dieu. Elle a reçu le pouvoir de faire ce qu’elle voulait pendant quarante-deux mois.

es.L: Y se le dio una boca que hablaba grandes cosas y blasfemias, y se le dio autoridad para actuar cuarenta y dos meses.
es.B: Se le permitió tener una boca que decía palabras arrogantes y blasfemias, y se le dio autoridad para actuar durante cuarenta y dos meses.
es.R: A la bestia se le permitió decir cosas orgullosas e insultar a Dios. Se le dio poder para hacer lo que quisiera durante cuarenta y dos meses.

sw.L: Na akapewa kinywa kinachosema mambo makuu na makufuru, naye akapewa mamlaka ya kutenda miezi arobaini na miwili.
sw.B: Aliruhusiwa kuwa na kinywa cha kusema maneno ya majivuno na makufuru, akapewa mamlaka ya kutenda kwa miezi arobaini na miwili.
sw.R: Mnyama huyo aliruhusiwa kusema maneno ya kiburi na kumtukana Mungu. Alipewa uwezo wa kufanya alivyotaka kwa miezi arobaini na miwili.

decisions.choice: a mouth speaking great things: Daniel's little horn
decisions.reason: Daniel's little horn had "a mouth speaking great things" and spoke words against the Most High; the saints were given into its hand for a time, times and half a time (Daniel 7:8, 20, 25). Forty-two months is the same span (11:2; 12:6, 14).

decisions.choice: was given: within God's limits
decisions.reason: The repeated "was given" (13:5, 7, 14, 15) shows that the beast acts only for the time and within the bounds God allows.

source.text: καὶ ἤνοιξε τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εἰς βλασφημίας πρὸς τὸν θεόν, βλασφημῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας.

records.literal_gloss: And it opened the mouth of it for blasphemies toward the God, to blaspheme the name of him and the tent of him, those in the heaven dwelling.

en.L: And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling, those who dwell in heaven.
en.B: Its mouth opened in blasphemies against God, insulting {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling, those whose home is in heaven.
en.R: It began to say insulting things against God. It insulted God's name and the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, and everyone who lives in heaven.

fr.L: Et elle ouvrit sa bouche en blasphèmes contre Dieu, pour blasphémer {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} demeure, ceux qui demeurent dans le ciel.
fr.B: Sa bouche s’ouvrit en blasphèmes contre Dieu : elle insulta {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} demeure, ceux qui ont leur demeure dans le ciel.
fr.R: Elle s’est mise à dire des insultes contre Dieu. Elle a insulté le nom de Dieu et le lieu où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} habite, et tous ceux qui habitent dans le ciel.

es.L: Y abrió su boca en blasfemias contra Dios, para blasfemar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada, a los que moran en el cielo.
es.B: Abrió la boca para blasfemar contra Dios, insultando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada, a los que tienen su hogar en el cielo.
es.R: Comenzó a decir insultos contra Dios. Insultó el nombre de Dios y el lugar donde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vive, y a todos los que viven en el cielo.

sw.L: Naye akafungua kinywa chake kwa makufuru dhidi ya Mungu, kulikufuru jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} na maskani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wale wanaokaa mbinguni.
sw.B: Kinywa chake kikafunguka kwa makufuru dhidi ya Mungu, akilitukana jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} na maskani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, yaani wale ambao makao yao ni mbinguni.
sw.R: Alianza kusema maneno ya matusi dhidi ya Mungu. Alilitukana jina la Mungu na mahali anapoishi, na kila mtu anayeishi mbinguni.

decisions.choice: his dwelling, those who dwell in heaven
alternatives: his dwelling and those who dwell in heaven, as two objects
decisions.reason: σκηνὴν is God's tent or dwelling (compare 21:3). The phrase that follows most likely explains it: God's dwelling is his people with him in heaven. Some manuscripts add "and", making them two objects.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada
decisions.reason: The Greek word is God's tent, the place where he dwells, and the clause after it names those who dwell there, as the meaning decision says; "morada" and "moran" keep the two words linked in Spanish as in the Greek. In Readable the English "he" is written as a stressed pronoun after "donde", so it carries the span.

decisions.choice: maskani
decisions.reason: The Greek word is God's tent, his dwelling (m1); Swahili "maskani" (dwelling place) gives the sense without the picture of a tent, which would read as a camp.

source.text: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων καὶ νικῆσαι αὐτούς, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν φυλὴν καὶ λαὸν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ ἔθνος.

records.literal_gloss: And it was given to it to make war with the saints and to overcome them, and was given to it authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation.

en.L: And it was allowed to make war with the saints and to overcome them, and authority was given to it over every tribe and people and language and nation.
en.B: It was allowed to make war on God's holy people and to overcome them; and authority was given to it over every tribe and people and language and nation.
en.R: It was allowed to fight against God's people and to defeat them. It was given power over every tribe, people, language, and nation.

fr.L: Et il lui fut donné de faire la guerre aux saints et de les vaincre, et il lui fut donné autorité sur toute tribu et peuple et langue et nation.
fr.B: Il lui fut permis de faire la guerre au peuple saint de Dieu et de le vaincre ; et elle reçut autorité sur toute tribu, tout peuple, toute langue et toute nation.
fr.R: Elle a pu combattre le peuple de Dieu et le vaincre. Elle a reçu le pouvoir sur toutes les tribus, tous les peuples, toutes les langues et toutes les nations.

es.L: Y se le concedió hacer guerra contra los santos y vencerlos, y se le dio autoridad sobre toda tribu y pueblo y lengua y nación.
es.B: Se le permitió hacer la guerra al pueblo santo de Dios y vencerlo, y se le dio autoridad sobre toda tribu, pueblo, lengua y nación.
es.R: Se le permitió pelear contra el pueblo de Dios y derrotarlo. Se le dio poder sobre toda tribu, pueblo, lengua y nación.

sw.L: Na akapewa [ruhusa] kufanya vita na watakatifu na kuwashinda, naye akapewa mamlaka juu ya kila kabila na watu na lugha na taifa.
sw.B: Aliruhusiwa kupigana vita na watu watakatifu wa Mungu na kuwashinda, akapewa mamlaka juu ya kila kabila, jamii, lugha na taifa.
sw.R: Aliruhusiwa kupigana na watu wa Mungu na kuwashinda. Alipewa mamlaka juu ya kila kabila, jamii, lugha na taifa.

decisions.choice: war on the saints: Daniel 7:21
decisions.reason: Daniel's horn "made war with the saints and prevailed over them" until God gave judgment (Daniel 7:21-22). νικῆσαι is the "overcome" of the letters: the beast seems to win, but the saints overcome by faithful witness (12:11; 15:2).

decisions.choice: the first clause is present
alternatives: the clause "it was allowed to make war with the saints and to overcome them" is missing
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts leave out the first clause, perhaps by an accidental skip from one "and it was given" to the next. The SBLGNT includes it, and the translation follows it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

decisions.choice: les saints (L); le peuple saint de Dieu (B); le peuple de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: As the French term sheet (§9) and the English: in modern French "les saints" suggests canonised individuals, so Balanced and Readable say who they are. The same in 13:10.

source.text: καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, οὗ οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου τοῦ ἐσφαγμένου ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: And will worship it all those dwelling on the earth, of whom not has been written the name of him in the book of the life of the Lamb the [one] having been slaughtered from foundation of world.

en.L: And all who live on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who was slaughtered.
en.B: All who live on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written, since the world was founded, in the book of life belonging to the Lamb who was slaughtered.
en.R: All the people on earth will worship the beast. These are the people whose names were not written in the book of life before the world was made. The book of life belongs to the Lamb who was killed.

fr.L: Et tous ceux qui habitent sur la terre l’adoreront, quiconque n’a pas eu son nom écrit, depuis la fondation du monde, dans le livre de vie de l’Agneau qui a été égorgé.
fr.B: Tous les habitants de la terre l’adoreront, tous ceux dont le nom n’a pas été écrit, depuis la création du monde, dans le livre de vie qui appartient à l’Agneau égorgé.
fr.R: Tous les gens de la terre adoreront la bête. Ce sont ceux dont le nom n’a pas été écrit dans le livre de vie avant la création du monde. Le livre de vie appartient à l’Agneau qui a été tué.

es.L: Y la adorarán todos los que habitan sobre la tierra, todo aquel cuyo nombre no ha sido escrito desde la fundación del mundo en el libro de la vida del Cordero que fue degollado.
es.B: La adorarán todos los habitantes de la tierra, todos aquellos cuyo nombre no ha sido escrito, desde la creación del mundo, en el libro de la vida que pertenece al Cordero que fue degollado.
es.R: Toda la gente de la tierra adorará a la bestia. Son las personas cuyos nombres no fueron escritos en el libro de la vida antes de que el mundo fuera hecho. El libro de la vida pertenece al Cordero que fue sacrificado.

sw.L: Na watamwabudu wote wanaokaa juu ya dunia, kila ambaye jina lake halijaandikwa tangu kuumbwa kwa ulimwengu katika kitabu cha uzima cha Mwanakondoo aliyechinjwa.
sw.B: Wote wanaoishi duniani watamwabudu, kila mtu ambaye jina lake halijaandikwa, tangu ulimwengu ulipowekewa misingi, katika kitabu cha uzima cha Mwanakondoo aliyechinjwa.
sw.R: Watu wote wa duniani watamwabudu mnyama huyo. Hao ndio watu ambao majina yao hayakuandikwa katika kitabu cha uzima kabla ulimwengu haujaumbwa. Kitabu hicho cha uzima ni cha Mwanakondoo aliyeuawa.

decisions.choice: "from the foundation of the world" goes with "written"
alternatives: it goes with "slaughtered": the Lamb slaughtered from the foundation of the world
decisions.reason: The phrase stands at the end of the sentence, after "the Lamb who was slaughtered", and could describe the Lamb's death as planned from before creation (compare 1 Peter 1:19-20). But Revelation 17:8 uses the same phrase of names "not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world", which favors taking it with "written" here too. The words of the sentence allow both.

decisions.choice: the book of life of the Lamb
decisions.reason: See the note on 3:5. The book belongs to the Lamb who was slaughtered: those written in it are those he redeemed (5:9).

decisions.choice: the phrase placed by "written" (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: To follow the punctuation decision (m1), every level puts "from the foundation of the world" next to "written", where English can show what it modifies.

decisions.choice: el libro de la vida
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is the one rendered "rollo" elsewhere in the book, but in this phrase it is the register of God's people, and "el libro de la vida" is the name Spanish readers know for it, as in 3:5. The phrase "from the foundation of the world" is placed beside "escrito", as the English places it.

decisions.choice: kitabu cha uzima
decisions.reason: The book of life (m2) is called "kitabu cha uzima", as in 3:5; "gombo" stays for the scroll of chapters 5 and 10.

source.text: Εἴ τις ἔχει οὖς ἀκουσάτω.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone has an ear, let him hear.

en.L: If anyone has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear.
en.B: If anyone has ears, let {{gender:them|him}} listen.
en.R: Anyone who can hear should listen carefully.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un a une oreille, qu’il entende.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un a des oreilles, qu’il écoute !
fr.R: Que celui qui peut entendre écoute bien !

es.L: Si alguien tiene oído, que oiga.
es.B: Si alguien tiene oídos, que escuche.
es.R: Todo el que pueda oír, que escuche con atención.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote aliye na sikio, na asikie.
sw.B: Kila mwenye masikio na asikilize.
sw.R: Kila anayeweza kusikia na asikilize kwa makini.

decisions.choice: the call of the seven letters
decisions.reason: The call that closed each letter (2:7) returns, now without "what the Spirit says to the churches": what follows is a warning for every hearer.

decisions.choice: "qu’il entende", "qu’il écoute" with no gender span; likewise "il va", "il doit" in 13:10
decisions.reason: Where the English needs {{gender:that person|him}} for the pronoun after "anyone", the French "quelqu’un … il" is already generic, so the French style guide (§7) puts no span on it.

decisions.choice: no gender span; wording as in 2:7
alternatives: a gender span, as in the English
decisions.reason: The call that closes the seven letters (m1), in the same Swahili as there; the verb prefix "a-" is free of gender, so the English span has no counterpart. The same in 13:10.

source.text: εἴ τις εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν, εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν ὑπάγει· εἴ τις ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone into captivity, into captivity he goes; if anyone with sword to be killed, him with sword to be killed.

en.L: If anyone [is] for captivity, into captivity {{gender:that person|he}} goes; if anyone [is] to be killed with the sword, with the sword {{gender:that person|he}} [is] to be killed.
en.B: Whoever is bound for captivity goes into captivity; whoever is to die by the sword must die by the sword.
en.R: Some people will be taken away as prisoners. That is what will happen to them. Some people will be killed with swords. That is what will happen to them.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un [est destiné] à la captivité, il va en captivité ; si quelqu’un [doit] être tué par l’épée, il [doit] être tué par l’épée.
fr.B: Qui est destiné à la captivité va en captivité ; qui doit mourir par l’épée doit mourir par l’épée.
fr.R: Certains seront emmenés comme prisonniers. C’est ce qui leur arrivera. Certains seront tués à l’épée. C’est ce qui leur arrivera.

es.L: Si alguien [está destinado] a la cautividad, a la cautividad va; si alguien [ha de] ser muerto a espada, a espada [ha de] ser muerto.
es.B: Quien esté destinado a la cautividad, a la cautividad irá; quien haya de morir a espada, a espada tendrá que morir.
es.R: Algunas personas serán llevadas como prisioneras. Eso es lo que les pasará. Algunas personas serán muertas a espada. Eso es lo que les pasará.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote [aliye wa] kifungoni, anakwenda kifungoni; mtu yeyote [aliye wa] kuuawa kwa upanga, kwa upanga [ni lazima] auawe.
sw.B: Yeyote anayepangiwa kifungo atakwenda kifungoni; yeyote atakayeuawa kwa upanga ni lazima auawe kwa upanga.
sw.R: Watu wengine watachukuliwa kuwa wafungwa. Hivyo ndivyo itakavyowapata. Watu wengine watauawa kwa upanga. Hivyo ndivyo itakavyowapata.

decisions.choice: captivity and the sword: Jeremiah 15:2
decisions.reason: God told Jeremiah: "Those for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; those for captivity, to captivity" (Jeremiah 15:2; 43:11). Believers must accept what is coming to them without escaping into compromise.

decisions.choice: if anyone is to be killed by the sword, by the sword they must be killed
alternatives: if anyone kills with the sword, by the sword they must be killed
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the passive, "to be killed", following Jeremiah. Other manuscripts read "if anyone kills with the sword", which makes it a warning against using violence, as in Matthew 26:52. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

source.text: ὧδέ ἐστιν ἡ ὑπομονὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις τῶν ἁγίων.

records.literal_gloss: Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.

en.L: Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.
en.B: Here is where God's holy people need endurance and faith.
en.R: This is why God's people must keep going and keep their faith.

fr.L: C’est ici l’endurance et la foi des saints.
fr.B: C’est ici que le peuple saint de Dieu a besoin d’endurance et de foi.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi le peuple de Dieu doit tenir bon et garder la foi.

es.L: Aquí está la perseverancia y la fe de los santos.
es.B: En esto el pueblo santo de Dios necesita perseverancia y fe.
es.R: Por eso el pueblo de Dios tiene que seguir adelante y mantenerse fiel.

sw.L: Hapa ndipo ulipo uvumilivu na imani ya watakatifu.
sw.B: Hapa ndipo watu watakatifu wa Mungu wanapohitaji uvumilivu na imani.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu watu wa Mungu wanapaswa kuendelea kustahimili na kudumu katika imani yao.

decisions.choice: faith: trust that holds firm, faithfulness
decisions.reason: πίστις can mean faith or faithfulness. Beside "endurance" it means the trust that keeps believers faithful under pressure (compare 14:12).

decisions.choice: here: in this situation
decisions.reason: "Here" points to the beast's power just described: this is where the saints' endurance and faith are needed and shown.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

source.text: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ εἶχεν κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὡς δράκων.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had horns two like to a lamb, and it was speaking as a dragon.

en.L: And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
en.B: I saw yet another beast coming up from the land. Its two horns were like a lamb's, yet its voice was the voice of a dragon.
en.R: Then I saw another beast coming up out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb. But it talked like a dragon.

fr.L: Et je vis une autre bête montant de la terre, et elle avait deux cornes semblables à un agneau, et elle parlait comme un dragon.
fr.B: Puis je vis une autre bête qui montait de la terre. Elle avait deux cornes semblables à celles d’un agneau, mais elle parlait comme un dragon.
fr.R: Puis j’ai vu une autre bête qui sortait du sol. Elle avait deux cornes comme un agneau. Mais elle parlait comme un dragon.

es.L: Y vi otra bestia que subía de la tierra, y tenía dos cuernos semejantes a [los de] un cordero, y hablaba como dragón.
es.B: Vi también otra bestia que subía de la tierra. Sus dos cuernos eran como los de un cordero, pero hablaba como un dragón.
es.R: Luego vi otra bestia que salía de la tierra. Tenía dos cuernos como los de un cordero. Pero hablaba como un dragón.

sw.L: Na nikamwona mnyama mwingine akipanda kutoka katika nchi, naye alikuwa na pembe mbili kama mwanakondoo, naye alikuwa akinena kama joka.
sw.B: Nikamwona mnyama mwingine akipanda kutoka katika nchi. Pembe zake mbili zilikuwa kama za mwanakondoo, lakini sauti yake ilikuwa sauti ya joka.
sw.R: Kisha nikamwona mnyama mwingine akitoka ardhini. Alikuwa na pembe mbili kama mwanakondoo. Lakini aliongea kama joka.

decisions.choice: the second beast: the false prophet
decisions.reason: Later this beast is called "the false prophet" (16:13; 19:20). It looks harmless, like a lamb, but speaks for the dragon. Jesus warned of false prophets who come in sheep's clothing (Matthew 7:15). It may stand for the religious and civic powers that promoted the worship of the emperor in Asia.

decisions.choice: out of the earth: from the land, in contrast to the sea
decisions.reason: γῆς can mean earth or land. The first beast came from the sea, this one from the land; together they cover the world.

decisions.choice: mwanakondoo (lowercase)
decisions.reason: Here the word is a comparison, a lamb's horns, so it is lowercase; the capital "Mwanakondoo" is kept for the title of Jesus (5:6). The likeness is deliberate: a false lamb.

source.text: καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πρώτου θηρίου πᾶσαν ποιεῖ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the authority of the first beast all it exercises before it.

en.L: And it exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence.
en.B: All the authority of the first beast it puts to use, acting in its presence.
en.R: It used all the power of the first beast, working for it.

fr.L: Et elle exerce toute l’autorité de la première bête en sa présence.
fr.B: Elle exerçait toute l’autorité de la première bête, en agissant en sa présence.
fr.R: Elle a utilisé tout le pouvoir de la première bête, en travaillant pour elle.

es.L: Y ejerce toda la autoridad de la primera bestia en su presencia.
es.B: Ejerce toda la autoridad de la primera bestia, actuando en su presencia.
es.R: Usaba todo el poder de la primera bestia y trabajaba para ella.

sw.L: Naye anatumia mamlaka yote ya yule mnyama wa kwanza mbele yake.
sw.B: Anatumia mamlaka yote ya mnyama wa kwanza, akitenda mbele yake.
sw.R: Alitumia uwezo wote wa mnyama wa kwanza, akimfanyia kazi.

decisions.choice: before it: in its presence, on its behalf
decisions.reason: ἐνώπιον means "in front of". The second beast acts as the first beast's servant and representative.

source.text: καὶ ποιεῖ τὴν γῆν καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικοῦντας ἵνα προσκυνήσουσιν τὸ θηρίον τὸ πρῶτον, οὗ ἐθεραπεύθη ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And it makes the earth and those in it dwelling that they will worship the beast the first, of whom was healed the wound of the death of it.

en.L: And it makes the earth and those who live in it worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.
en.B: It forces the earth and its people to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.
en.R: It made everyone on earth worship the first beast, the one whose deadly wound had healed.

fr.L: Et elle fait que la terre et ceux qui y habitent adorent la première bête, dont la blessure mortelle fut guérie.
fr.B: Elle forçait la terre et ses habitants à adorer la première bête, celle dont la blessure mortelle avait été guérie.
fr.R: Elle a obligé tous les habitants de la terre à adorer la première bête, celle dont la blessure mortelle avait guéri.

es.L: Y hace que la tierra y los que habitan en ella adoren a la primera bestia, cuya herida de muerte fue sanada.
es.B: Obliga a la tierra y a sus habitantes a adorar a la primera bestia, cuya herida mortal fue sanada.
es.R: Hizo que todos en la tierra adoraran a la primera bestia, la que tenía la herida mortal que se había curado.

sw.L: Naye anaifanya dunia na wale wanaokaa ndani yake wamwabudu yule mnyama wa kwanza, ambaye jeraha lake la kifo lilipona.
sw.B: Analazimisha dunia na watu wake wamwabudu mnyama wa kwanza, ambaye jeraha lake la kuua lilipona.
sw.R: Aliwalazimisha watu wote duniani wamwabudu mnyama wa kwanza, yule ambaye jeraha lake la kuua lilikuwa limepona.

decisions.choice: a false religion that points to the beast
decisions.reason: The second beast does for the first what the Spirit does for Christ: it draws worship to him. Revelation exposes the worship of earthly power as idolatry.

source.text: καὶ ποιεῖ σημεῖα μεγάλα, ἵνα καὶ πῦρ ποιῇ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνειν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: And it does signs great, so that even fire it makes out of the heaven to come down to the earth before the men.

en.L: And it performs great signs, so that it even makes fire come down from heaven to the earth in the sight of {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: It performs great signs, even bringing fire down from the sky to the earth in front of everyone.
en.R: It did great miracles, called signs. It even made fire come down from the sky to the earth while people watched.

fr.L: Et elle fait de grands signes, au point de faire même descendre du feu du ciel sur la terre, aux yeux des {{gender:humains|hommes}}.
fr.B: Elle accomplissait de grands signes, faisant même descendre du feu du ciel sur la terre devant tout le monde.
fr.R: Elle a fait de grands signes, des choses extraordinaires. Elle a même fait descendre du feu du ciel sur la terre, sous les yeux des gens.

es.L: Y hace grandes señales, de tal manera que aun hace descender fuego del cielo a la tierra delante de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.
es.B: Hace grandes señales, incluso hace bajar fuego del cielo a la tierra a la vista de todos.
es.R: Hacía grandes milagros, llamados señales. Hasta hacía bajar fuego del cielo a la tierra mientras la gente miraba.

sw.L: Naye anafanya ishara kubwa, hata kufanya moto ushuke kutoka mbinguni hadi duniani mbele ya watu.
sw.B: Anafanya ishara kubwa, hata kushusha moto kutoka angani hadi duniani mbele ya watu wote.
sw.R: Alifanya miujiza mikubwa, inayoitwa ishara. Hata alifanya moto ushuke kutoka angani hadi duniani watu wakiona.

decisions.choice: fire from heaven: a counterfeit of Elijah
decisions.reason: Elijah called down fire from heaven to show that the LORD is God (1 Kings 18:38), and the two witnesses have fire from their mouths (11:5). The second beast imitates the signs of God's prophets. Moses warned against prophets who give signs and lead to other gods (Deuteronomy 13:1-3), and Jesus and Paul warned of false signs (Mark 13:22; 2 Thessalonians 2:9).

decisions.choice: signs; miracles, called signs (R)
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term and stays. Readable adds what the signs were.

decisions.choice: de grands signes, des choses extraordinaires (R)
alternatives: de grands miracles, qu’on appelle des signes
decisions.reason: The French term sheet never uses "miracle" for sign; Readable keeps "signes" and says what they were with "des choses extraordinaires", as the English Readable adds what the signs were.

decisions.choice: miujiza ..., inayoitwa ishara (R)
decisions.reason: "Ishara" (sign) at Literal and Balanced, as in 12:1; Readable says "miracles, called signs", as the English Readable does, the one place where "muujiza" is used, and only to explain the word.

source.text: καὶ πλανᾷ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς διὰ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θηρίου, λέγων τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ποιῆσαι εἰκόνα τῷ θηρίῳ, ὃς ἔχει τὴν πληγὴν τῆς μαχαίρης καὶ ἔζησεν.

records.literal_gloss: And it deceives those dwelling on the earth because of the signs which were given to it to do before the beast, telling those dwelling on the earth to make an image to the beast, which has the wound of the sword and lived.

en.L: And it deceives those who live on the earth by the signs that it was allowed to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who live on the earth to make an image for the beast that has the wound of the sword and came to life.
en.B: It leads astray the people of the earth with the signs it was allowed to do in the beast's presence, and it tells them to make an image for the beast that had the sword-wound and yet came back to life.
en.R: It fooled the people on earth with the signs it was allowed to do for the first beast. It told them to make a statue to honor the beast that had been wounded by a sword and yet lived.

fr.L: Et elle égare ceux qui habitent sur la terre par les signes qu’il lui fut donné de faire en présence de la bête, disant à ceux qui habitent sur la terre de faire une image pour la bête qui a la blessure de l’épée et qui reprit vie.
fr.B: Par les signes qu’il lui était donné d’accomplir en présence de la bête, elle égarait les habitants de la terre, et elle leur disait de faire une image en l’honneur de la bête qui avait reçu le coup d’épée et qui pourtant était revenue à la vie.
fr.R: Elle a trompé les gens de la terre avec les signes qu’elle avait le droit de faire pour la première bête. Elle leur a dit de faire une statue en l’honneur de la bête qui avait été blessée par l’épée et qui pourtant était vivante.

es.L: Y engaña a los que habitan sobre la tierra por las señales que se le concedió hacer en presencia de la bestia, diciendo a los que habitan sobre la tierra que hagan una imagen a la bestia que tiene la herida de la espada y revivió.
es.B: Engaña a la gente de la tierra con las señales que se le permitió hacer en presencia de la bestia, y le dice que haga una imagen en honor de la bestia que fue herida a espada y, sin embargo, volvió a vivir.
es.R: Engañó a la gente de la tierra con las señales que se le permitió hacer delante de la primera bestia. Les dijo que hicieran una estatua para honrar a la bestia que había sido herida con una espada y, aun así, vivió.

sw.L: Naye anawadanganya wale wanaokaa juu ya dunia kwa ishara alizopewa kuzifanya mbele ya mnyama, akiwaambia wale wanaokaa juu ya dunia wamfanyie sanamu mnyama yule aliye na jeraha la upanga naye akaishi.
sw.B: Anawapotosha watu wa dunia kwa ishara alizoruhusiwa kuzifanya mbele ya mnyama, akiwaambia wamtengenezee sanamu mnyama yule aliyekuwa na jeraha la upanga lakini akarudi kuishi.
sw.R: Aliwadanganya watu wa duniani kwa ishara alizoruhusiwa kuzifanya kwa ajili ya mnyama wa kwanza. Aliwaambia watengeneze sanamu ya kumheshimu mnyama yule aliyejeruhiwa kwa upanga lakini akaishi.

decisions.choice: an image: a statue for worship
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and commanded all to worship it (Daniel 3). In the cities of Asia there were temples and statues of the emperors, where offerings were made.

decisions.choice: wounded and came to life: the beast's false resurrection
decisions.reason: ἔζησεν is the verb used of Christ, "who was dead and came to life" (2:8). The beast mimics the resurrection (13:3).

decisions.choice: image (L, B); statue (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word for what was set up.

decisions.choice: imagen (L, B); estatua (R)
decisions.reason: The image is a statue made for worship, as the meaning decision says. "Imagen" keeps the Greek word, which recurs through the book; Readable says "estatua", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: sanamu
decisions.reason: "Sanamu" (a statue, an image for worship), the word used for idols in 9:20 (m1); it serves for both the English "image" and the Readable "statue".

source.text: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ δοῦναι πνεῦμα τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου, ἵνα καὶ λαλήσῃ ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ποιήσῃ ἵνα ὅσοι ἐὰν μὴ προσκυνήσωσιν τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου ἀποκτανθῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And it was given to it to give breath to the image of the beast, so that also might speak the image of the beast and might cause that as many as if not would worship the image of the beast be killed.

en.L: And it was allowed to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast would even speak and would cause as many as do not worship the image of the beast to be killed.
en.B: It was permitted to give life-breath to the image of the beast, so that the image could even speak, and could have put to death all who refused to worship it.
en.R: It was allowed to give breath to the statue of the beast, so that the statue could talk. The statue ordered that everyone who would not worship it must be killed.

fr.L: Et il lui fut donné de donner un souffle à l’image de la bête, afin que l’image de la bête parle même, et fasse que tous ceux qui n’adoreraient pas l’image de la bête soient tués.
fr.B: Il lui fut permis d’animer d’un souffle l’image de la bête, si bien que l’image pouvait même parler, et faire mettre à mort tous ceux qui refusaient de l’adorer.
fr.R: Elle a reçu le droit de donner un souffle à la statue de la bête, pour que la statue puisse parler. La statue a ordonné de tuer tous ceux qui refusaient de l’adorer.

es.L: Y se le concedió dar aliento a la imagen de la bestia, para que la imagen de la bestia también hablara e hiciera que fueran muertos todos los que no adoraran la imagen de la bestia.
es.B: Se le permitió dar aliento de vida a la imagen de la bestia, de modo que la imagen pudiera incluso hablar y mandar matar a todos los que se negaran a adorarla.
es.R: Se le permitió darle aliento a la estatua de la bestia, para que la estatua pudiera hablar. La estatua ordenó que mataran a todos los que no la adoraran.

sw.L: Naye akapewa [ruhusa] kuipa pumzi sanamu ya mnyama, ili sanamu ya mnyama hata inene na kufanya kwamba wote wasioiabudu sanamu ya mnyama wauawe.
sw.B: Aliruhusiwa kuipa sanamu ya mnyama pumzi ya uhai, ili sanamu hiyo iweze hata kusema, na kuwafanya wauawe wote waliokataa kuiabudu.
sw.R: Aliruhusiwa kuipa pumzi sanamu ya mnyama, ili sanamu hiyo iweze kuongea. Sanamu hiyo iliamuru kwamba kila mtu asiyeiabudu lazima auawe.

decisions.choice: death for refusing to worship: Daniel 3
decisions.reason: Those who would not bow to Nebuchadnezzar's image were to be thrown into the furnace (Daniel 3:6). Pliny the Younger, governor of a neighboring province around AD 112, wrote that he executed Christians who would not offer wine and incense to the emperor's image.

decisions.choice: a speaking image
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα is breath or spirit. The second beast makes the image seem alive, a false likeness of God giving the breath of life (11:11). Ancient writers describe tricks that made statues seem to speak.

source.text: καὶ ποιεῖ πάντας, τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς, καὶ τοὺς ἐλευθέρους καὶ τοὺς δούλους, ἵνα δῶσιν αὐτοῖς χάραγμα ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς ἢ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῶν, καὶ ἵνα μή τις δύνηται ἀγοράσαι ἢ πωλῆσαι εἰ μὴ ὁ ἔχων τὸ χάραγμα, τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θηρίου ἢ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And it makes all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free and the slaves, that they give them a mark on the hand of them the right or on the forehead of them, \v 17 and that not anyone may be able to buy or to sell except the [one] having the mark, the name of the beast or the number of the name of it.

en.L: And it causes all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free and the slaves, to be given a mark on their right hand or on their forehead, \v 17 so that no one can buy or sell except the one who has the mark, the name of the beast or the number of its name.
en.B: It makes everyone, the lowly and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slave, take a mark on the right hand or on the forehead. \v 17 No one may buy or sell except those who have the mark: the name of the beast or the number that stands for its name.
en.R: It forced all people to have a mark put on their right hand or on their forehead. It did this to important and unimportant people, rich and poor, free people and slaves. \v 17 No one could buy or sell anything without this mark. The mark was the name of the beast or the number of its name.

fr.L: Et elle fait en sorte qu’à tous, les petits et les grands, et les riches et les pauvres, et les libres et les esclaves, on donne une marque sur leur main droite ou sur leur front, \v 17 et que personne ne puisse acheter ou vendre, sinon celui qui a la marque, le nom de la bête ou le nombre de son nom.
fr.B: Elle obligeait tout le monde, petits et grands, riches et pauvres, libres et esclaves, à recevoir une marque sur la main droite ou sur le front. \v 17 Personne ne pouvait acheter ni vendre, sauf ceux qui portaient la marque : le nom de la bête ou le nombre qui représente son nom.
fr.R: Elle a obligé tout le monde à se faire mettre une marque sur la main droite ou sur le front. Elle l’a fait pour les gens importants et les gens sans importance, pour les riches et les pauvres, pour les gens libres et les esclaves. \v 17 Personne ne pouvait rien acheter ni vendre sans cette marque. La marque, c’était le nom de la bête ou le nombre de son nom.

es.L: Y hace que a todos, a los pequeños y a los grandes, a los ricos y a los pobres, a los libres y a los esclavos, se les ponga una marca en la mano derecha o en la frente, \v 17 y que nadie pueda comprar ni vender sino el que tiene la marca, el nombre de la bestia o el número de su nombre.
es.B: Obliga a todos, pequeños y grandes, ricos y pobres, libres y esclavos, a recibir una marca en la mano derecha o en la frente, \v 17 de modo que nadie pueda comprar ni vender si no tiene la marca, que es el nombre de la bestia o el número de su nombre.
es.R: Obligó a todas las personas a que les pusieran una marca en la mano derecha o en la frente. Lo hizo con la gente importante y con la gente sencilla, con los ricos y con los pobres, con los libres y con los esclavos. \v 17 Nadie podía comprar ni vender nada sin esa marca. La marca era el nombre de la bestia o el número de su nombre.

sw.L: Naye anawafanya wote, wadogo na wakubwa, na matajiri na maskini, na walio huru na watumwa, wapewe chapa juu ya mkono wao wa kulia au juu ya kipaji cha uso wao, \v 17 ili mtu yeyote asiweze kununua wala kuuza isipokuwa yule aliye na chapa, yaani jina la mnyama au hesabu ya jina lake.
sw.B: Anawalazimisha watu wote, wanyonge na wakubwa, matajiri na maskini, walio huru na watumwa, watiwe chapa kwenye mkono wa kulia au kwenye kipaji cha uso. \v 17 Hakuna mtu awezaye kununua wala kuuza isipokuwa wale walio na chapa hiyo, yaani jina la mnyama au hesabu inayosimama kwa jina lake.
sw.R: Aliwalazimisha watu wote watiwe alama kwenye mkono wa kulia au kwenye kipaji cha uso. Alifanya hivyo kwa watu wa maana na wasio na maana, matajiri na maskini, watu huru na watumwa. \v 17 Hakuna mtu aliyeweza kununua wala kuuza kitu chochote bila alama hiyo. Alama hiyo ilikuwa jina la mnyama au hesabu ya jina lake.

decisions.choice: a mark: a brand or stamp of ownership, a counterfeit of God's seal
decisions.reason: χάραγμα was used of a brand on slaves or animals and of the imperial stamp on documents and coins. God's slaves are sealed on the forehead (7:3; 14:1); the beast's followers bear its mark. Whether it is a visible mark or a picture of allegiance, it shows whom a person belongs to.

decisions.choice: hand and forehead: a parody of God's words on the hand and between the eyes
decisions.reason: Israel was told to bind God's words "as a sign on your hand and as frontlets between your eyes" (Deuteronomy 6:8). The beast demands the same place for its mark: loyalty in deed and thought.

decisions.choice: no buying or selling: economic exclusion
decisions.reason: In the cities of Asia, trade guilds held feasts in honor of the gods and the emperor, and refusing to take part could cost believers their livelihood (compare 2:9, 2:20). The mark's power is economic as well as religious.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free.

decisions.choice: esclaves (B, R)
decisions.reason: The French term sheet says "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable except where slavery itself is the point; here slaves are set against the free, so every level says "esclaves", as the English does.

decisions.choice: una marca
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a brand or stamp, a different word from God's "sello" in 7:3, though it imitates it, as the meaning decision says. "Marca" keeps the two apart; "señal" is kept for the signs. The free are set against the slaves here, so "esclavos" stands at every level, as in 6:15.

decisions.choice: chapa (L, B); alama (R)
decisions.reason: "Chapa" is a brand or stamped mark of ownership (m1), kept apart from "muhuri", God's seal on his servants in 7:3, of which it is a counterfeit; Readable says the plain "alama" (mark). The same in 14:9-11.

decisions.choice: watumwa
decisions.reason: Here slavery itself is the point, slave and free, so "watumwa" at every level, as the Swahili New Testament does where the English keeps "slaves".

source.text: ὧδε ἡ σοφία ἐστίν· ὁ ἔχων νοῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου, ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν· καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτοῦ ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ.

records.literal_gloss: Here the wisdom is. The [one] having understanding let him count the number of the beast, for number of a man it is, and the number of it 666.

en.L: Here is wisdom: let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is [the] number of a human, and its number [is] 666.
en.B: Here wisdom is needed. Whoever has understanding should count up the number of the beast, for it is a human number. Its number is 666.
en.R: Here you need wisdom. If you are wise, you can figure out the number of the beast. It stands for a person. The number is 666.

fr.L: C’est ici la sagesse. Que celui qui a de l’intelligence calcule le nombre de la bête, car c’est [le] nombre d’un {{gender:être humain|homme}}, et son nombre [est] 666.
fr.B: Il faut ici de la sagesse. Que celui qui a de l’intelligence calcule le nombre de la bête, car c’est un nombre {{gender:humain|d’homme}}. Son nombre est 666.
fr.R: Ici, il faut de la sagesse. Celui qui est sage peut trouver le nombre de la bête. Il représente une personne. Ce nombre est 666.

es.L: Aquí está la sabiduría: el que tiene entendimiento, calcule el número de la bestia, porque es número de un ser humano, y su número [es] 666.
es.B: Aquí se necesita sabiduría. El que tenga entendimiento, que calcule el número de la bestia, porque es un número humano. Su número es 666.
es.R: Aquí hace falta sabiduría. El que sea sabio puede descifrar el número de la bestia. Representa a una persona. El número es 666.

sw.L: Hapa ndipo ilipo hekima: mwenye akili na aihesabu hesabu ya mnyama, kwa maana ni hesabu ya mwanadamu, na hesabu yake [ni] 666.
sw.B: Hapa hekima inahitajika. Mwenye akili na ahesabu hesabu ya mnyama, kwa maana ni hesabu ya kibinadamu. Hesabu yake ni 666.
sw.R: Hapa unahitaji hekima. Kama una hekima, unaweza kuifahamu hesabu ya mnyama. Inasimama kwa mtu. Hesabu hiyo ni 666.

decisions.choice: 666: a number that may spell a name
alternatives: the name of the emperor Nero, spelled in Hebrew letters
a number that falls short of seven, the number of completeness, three times over
a name that cannot now be known
decisions.reason: In Greek and Hebrew, letters were also numbers, and a name could be counted up. Spelled in Hebrew letters, the Greek title "Nero Caesar" adds up to 666, and a Latin spelling to 616 (see m2). Others take 666 as the number that falls short of seven at every point, the opposite of God's completeness. "The number of a man" can mean the number of a particular person or a human number. Many names have been proposed; John asks the reader for wisdom, not guessing.

The SBLGNT reads 666. A few early witnesses read 616, and Irenaeus, in the second century, knew of that reading and rejected it. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: 666 (numerals)
decisions.reason: The number is given in figures, as the style guide does for large numbers.

decisions.choice: "d’un {{gender:être humain|homme}}" (L); "un nombre {{gender:humain|d’homme}}" (B)
decisions.reason: The English says "a human" with no setting, but French must choose between "homme", the traditional rendering, and an inclusive word; the Greek is generic (anthrōpos), so the inclusive default carries the setting. Readable says "une personne", already inclusive.

decisions.choice: de un ser humano (L); humano (B); a una persona (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means a human being, and the English has no gender span here; Spanish says "ser humano" so it is not read as a man only. Readable says the number stands for a person, as the English does. Readable keeps the general third person ("el que sea sabio") where the English uses a general "you".

decisions.choice: hesabu
decisions.reason: "Hesabu" (number, a reckoning), which goes with the call to "kuhesabu" (count it up); the number may spell a name (m1). In figures, as the English has it.
